name: Milemarker
label: Jade Tree
lede: Milemarker started in Chapel Hill as a collective, set its drum kit on fire, then moved to Chicago to make synth-punk for Jade Tree with Steve Albini behind the board. It never announced a breakup, which is how a band ends up on a U.S. tour in 2017 with two members living in Germany.

eras.title: Casio presets and lighter fluid
eras.text: Milemarker began in Chapel Hill, North Carolina, as a self-declared collective, not a band, and made art-damaged hardcore out of synthesizers and slogans. It put out records at a sprint on small labels and lit its own stage.

years.src: Indy Week: This milepost · Jade Tree · Village Voice: Milemarker · Milemarker on Bandcamp
years.h: Three friends in Chapel Hill call it a collective, not a band
years.p: Dave Laney, Al Burian and Ben Davis describe Milemarker as sci-fi soundtrack music genetically spliced with [[Black Flag|9941a936-196a-4a62-ae53-a69cbc33f20e]]. Laney later called them the art-damaged kids of the scene.
years.xp:
Jade Tree's bio lists the collective's other names: the Milemarker People's Liberation Army and the Milemarker Entertainment and Reprogramming Consulate. The rule was that revolutionary art should be danceable.

Laney told the Village Voice: "We were sort of the art-damaged kids, making music in a different context with an art angle." The Casio presets put off hardcore purists. Laney edited the magazine Media Reader on the side, and Burian wrote the zine Burn Collector.

yt: Cedar Grove NJ Hardcore Fest, May 24, 1998
years.h: Non Plus Ultra and Future Isms land in the same year
years.p: Non Plus Ultra comes out on Paralogy and Future Isms on Stickfigure, with the Receiver 7-inch on Clocked Out alongside. The clip is a full set from the Cedar Grove NJ Hardcore Fest, May 24, 1998.

years.h: Seattle's Blood Brothers take the other side of a 7-inch
years.p: Milemarker splits it with [[The Blood Brothers|b847568f-cd75-44c7-b87b-4f38a5a9f661]]. The year also brings the Sex Jams 7-inch on Bloodlink and Changing Caring Humans on Stickfigure.

years.big: We were all setting everything on fire
years.src: Village Voice: Milemarker · Indy Week: This milepost
years.h: Ben Davis soaks his drums in lighter fluid and lights them mid-set
years.p: Al Burian told the Village Voice the stunts were a contest for attention, and breathing fire followed. Milemarker got banned from Chapel Hill's Cat's Cradle after smashing a keyboard.
years.xp:
When Roby Newton joined, she built a rig to set her arms alight; Indy Week says she also performed topless in electrical tape, among light boxes she had rigged herself.

Laney told Indy Week the point was service: "You pay $30 to see Iron Maiden and you get a show... Now you can pay $15 to see an indie band and they don't service you like that."

eras.title: Chicago, a new singer, and Jade Tree
eras.text: Milemarker moved to Chicago, where its lighting tech took over the microphone and the synth records found homes on Lovitt Records and Jade Tree. By 2001 the band was saying it had stopped being a spectacle and become a band.

yt: Live, Frigid Forms Sell You Warmth tour, 2001
years.h: Frigid Forms Sell comes out on Lovitt
years.p: Brian McTernan recorded it at Salad Days Studio; it's Lovitt LOV20. Songs include Sex Jam One: Sexual Machinery and Server Error.
years.xp: The credits list Al Burian, Dave Laney, Ben Davis, Roby Newton and drummer Sean Husick. Jade Tree reissued it in 2002, which is why Milemarker's Bandcamp dates it February 2002. Burian later called it the record with the most solid aesthetic and message.
play: Internet Relay Chat with the Central Intelligence Agency

years.cap: Al Burian at the Fireside Bowl, Chicago
years.src: Chicago Reader: Out Go · Indy Week: This milepost · Westword
years.h: Milemarker packs for Chicago, the last city standing
years.p: Everyone had wanted out of North Carolina for a long time, Dave Laney told the Chicago Reader, and Chicago won by elimination. The move came in 2000.
years.xp: Indy Week and Westword both date the move to 2000. The Chicago Reader, writing in 2001, puts it about a year earlier.

years.cap: Milemarker at Hampshire College, Amherst, Massachusetts
years.src: Chicago Reader: Out Go · Roy Christopher
years.h: Roby Newton runs the lights, then takes the microphone
years.p: [[Roby Newton|b8497e6d-09f9-4a5a-bab8-9a9496ae0af2]] joins to handle lighting and projections, then moves to vocals and synthesizer. She's also a puppeteer who tours her own shows and animations.

years.src: Discogs · Creative Loafing Tampa · Chicago Reader: Out Go · Roy Christopher
years.h: Anaesthetic is the first Jade Tree full-length
years.p: Brian McTernan recorded it at Salad Days Studio in Washington, D.C., May 8 to 20, 2001, and Jade Tree issued it as JT1061. The songs go after gentrification, sweatshops and terminal illness.
years.xp:
Burian said the album was first called Rise Up Friends, an animal-liberation concept the band dropped, and that three different drummers played on it. Demos were cut at [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]]'s Electrical Audio.

The release party was at Chicago's Fireside Bowl.

years.cap: Milemarker at El Paso, Torino, Italy
years.h: Noah Leger, formerly of Hurl, sits in on drums
years.p: The Chicago Reader listed [[Noah Leger|c8fd59fc-09db-4e77-9a67-749e5f47a3d6]], also of Thee Speaking Canaries, as the temporary drummer. He's still there for Ominosity.

years.src: Discogs · Milemarker on Bandcamp · Wikipedia: Milemarker
years.h: Satanic Versus goes to Steve Albini
years.p: [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]] recorded the three heavy songs at Electrical Audio on March 22 and 23, 2002 (Jade Tree JT1078). The electronic tracks that follow, the label said, recalled Kraftwerk and Prince.
years.xp: Noah Leger and Tim Herzog split the drums. Czech label Day After licensed a vinyl edition from Jade Tree. Pitchfork's Chris Ott reviewed it that October.

eras.title: Two years off, then Albini again
eras.text: In summer 2003 Milemarker stopped in a way the A.V. Club said looked more like a breakup. Two years later it returned with new members, a record made with Steve Albini and a harder, less synth-driven sound, just as synth-rock was getting popular.

years.src: A.V. Club: Milemarker · Indy Week: This milepost
years.h: Roby Newton leaves as Laney and Burian shelve Milemarker
years.p: Summer 2003: the two put the band aside for a new one. Davis told Indy Week that Newton didn't feel she was expressing herself fully.
years.xp: Davis added that she had been lighting herself on fire at the time. Indy Week reported that Newton went on to start a band with Rjyan Kidwell, who records as Cex.

years.h: The side band Challenger gets a record out first
years.p: Burian, Laney and Tim Remis make Give People What They Want in Lethal Doses, a harder rock record the A.V. Club filed under agit-punk.

years.src: Discogs · Indy Week: This milepost · A.V. Club: Milemarker
years.h: Ominosity brings Albini back, on a New Jersey label
years.p: Steve Albini and Greg Norman recorded it; Eyeball Records released it. Leger drums, and Monika Bukowska and Remis sing.
years.xp:
Indy Week called the sessions chaotic and rushed. Davis, who had left the band, flew in to play synthesizer, and recorded his parts in one exhausting session before sprinting to catch a flight after laying down a slide guitar part. Tony Lazzara plays second drums.

Burian told the A.V. Club that once you've done something, repeating it makes little sense.

years.src: Indy Week: This milepost · Wikipedia: Milemarker
years.h: Wetlands, $8 at the door, and then five quiet years
years.p: Indy Week previewed the Chapel Hill homecoming. Laney planned to move back to the Triangle after the tour, and Milemarker didn't record or tour again until 2008.

eras.title: Never broke up, so it could come back
eras.text: Milemarker never announced an ending, so it could return whenever it liked: a Chapel Hill show and a European tour in 2008. Then Al Burian, who has a German mother and German citizenship, moved to Berlin.

years.h: Chapel Hill gets Milemarker for the first time in two years
years.p: Punknews announced the reunion in May 2008. A 12-date European tour followed, with a festival in Lärz, Germany.

years.h: Burian trades Chicago for Berlin
years.p: He moves in spring 2010. That fall PM Press collects Burn Collector issues 1 to 9, his autobiographical zine about travel and bad apartments.
years.xp: Burian told Creative Loafing he grew up speaking German and holds German citizenship through his mother. He tells artists he's a musician and musicians he's a writer.

years.h: Laney starts Bee Control with a Pelican guitarist
years.p: Punknews premieres the project with Trevor de Brauw of [[Pelican|5a797e16-f69a-4957-820f-1152ec19d236]] and Theo Katsaounis of [[Joan of Arc|0f2fea44-7e03-47f9-86e6-91d0a22fd0ee]].

eras.title: Two members in Germany, one new album
eras.text: A short European tour in 2015 turned into new songs, Milemarker's first album in eleven years, and a U.S. tour at a moment when its dystopian themes sounded current.

years.h: A short European tour has Burian and Laney writing again
years.p: Lovitt Records puts out the Conditional Love 7-inch, Milemarker's first new music in a decade.

q: We're not At the Drive-In getting back together, you know?
years.h: Eleven years on, Overseas
years.p: Burian and Laney, now living in Germany, make it with drummer Ezra Cale and keyboardist Lena Kilkka. One song is named for Carrboro, next to Chapel Hill.
years.xp: The title points both at the move abroad and at the technology worries of the band's earlier records. Burian told the Village Voice: "I'm kind of surprised this is going on right now."

years.h: Denver's Marquis Theater, twenty years in
years.p: The Thursday, February 23 show is all ages, with Big Jesus and Too Many Humans, $12 to $14.
years.xp: Burian told Westword: "The band gets it a lot, because we were dystopian, and a lot of the themes we talked about really resonate right now." On technology: "We actually always embraced technology."
